logic.note: The DS3231 model of ds3231-rtc: I2C at 0x68, BCD time and date with century and 12/24-hour mode, the time latched at START, the oscillator-stop flag, control/aging registers and the temperature registers.

timing.note: The clock runs with simulation time, exactly (0 ppm). Writing the time restarts the second like the chip. Alarms are stored but never fire.

analog.note: Temperature is the temperature prop, rounded to 0.25 °C.

power.note: 0.11 mA from VCC (datasheet ICCS at 3.3 V); the 0.58 mA temperature conversion every 64 s is not added. The coin cell is not modelled: the time survives power loss and lostPower is a prop.

emulates: Registers 0x00-0x12 of the DS3231 (time, date, control, status, aging, temperature)
Setting the time (rtc.adjust) and the oscillator-stop flag (rtc.lostPower)
A scenario's clock and set_clock steps
doesNotEmulate: Alarms and the SQW / 32 kHz outputs (not broken out on this module)
testOnRealDevice: Which coin cell your module takes (CR1220 class on most; some sellers ship a rechargeable one) and that the time survives the board being unpowered
Whether your board has I2C pull-up resistors; with none, long wires need 4.7 kOhm to 3V3
The height once the socket is removed and wires are soldered
